messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: Can an interactive R learning environment be created using Shiny?
parts:
I had the same question a few months ago when I saw http://tryruby.org
At that time, I was hoping Rserve could do it but that was too
difficult for me.

Now I think shiny has the potential for building such an interactive
tutorial for R: find a JS library for emulating the console, use knitr
as the backend evaluator, markdown as the renderer, bind events of the
JS library to shiny, and we should be done. Perhaps it is not too
different with http://glimmer.rstudio.com/yihui/knitr/

I'd be excited to see someone implement it.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Can an interactive R learning environment be created using Shiny?
parts: You'd need to be very, very careful about the security implications though. In general if your Shiny process is evaluating code that's being passed to you from the user, that should be considered a giant security hole. It is and always has been easy to implement this sort of thing, the hard part is making it scalable, robust, and--especially--secure.

messages.subject: Re: Can an interactive R learning environment be created using Shiny?
parts:
Exactly. An alternative approach is to build it on top of OpenCPU,
which has addressed some of the security issues, but the problem is
(maybe I'm wrong) that you do not have an active R session listening
behind.

Or as the first step, do it locally with Shiny, and wait for the
security issues to be addressed in the future...

Regards,

messages.subject: Re: Can an interactive R learning environment be created using Shiny?
parts:
This is a great discussion. It will be great to be able to create lessons like in tryR codeschool easily. 

Anyway, for now I wanted to play with Shiny to see if some basic version of something like tryR can be done. This is by no means meant to be a robust, scalable way to implement something like tryR. This was more for me to use as an example to learn some Shiny.

I have uploaded the app to 

http://glimmer.rstudio.com/rdabbler/tstCoderun

The code used is stored in the following location

https://gist.github.com/4240980

Thanks,
Shankar
